answer: At most 3 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a umber tag. The saffron cap is upheld at intake and vertex shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, because each account consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 30 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
